findings: Coinbase has two distinct XRP collateral channels: USDC loans through Morpho on Base (stated up to $100K against XRP) and Global Exchange cross-collateral for perpetual futures; neither product page discloses actual XRP collateral utilization.
Circle USDC is native on XRPL but its reported on-ledger supply is only about 6.02M, while Ripple RLUSD is about 711.83M on XRPL; provider timestamps differ.
XRP/RLUSD AMM TVL is reported around $5.38M versus about $0.26M for USDC/XRP; AMM metrics exclude order-book liquidity and must not be treated as total XRPL liquidity.
Native XRPL lending remains inactive; vault/loan-broker metadata is not proof of live collateralized lending.
Circle and Ripple both invested in Flutterwave; current public API docs list RLUSD only on Ethereum and do not list XRPL, despite the earlier XRPL/RLUSD announcement.
Coinbase Q3 stablecoin revenue and Circle distribution costs are material business economics but not XRP-specific capital flows.
ASK remains a strong Permission Coin candidate with Coinbase embedded-wallet infrastructure and Base/Polygon token contracts; no direct XRPL link is verified.
Tokyo SBIC is a distinct SME investment corporation; ChatGPT/Copilot training was for investee companies, not an OpenAI commercial partnership.
